newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB urges farmers in flood plain to move grain.
newsitem.headline: CWB urges farmers in flood plain to move grain.

text.p: Red River Valley farmers may deliver more grain on the Canadian Wheat Board's first two quarterly contracts ahead of spring floods, the CWB said.
The CWB authorized flood zone farmers to deliver 80 percent of their first quarterly contracts and 60 percent of their second quarterly grain delivery contracts.
"Some grain has already been moved to the U.S. from southern Manitoba due to the vessel backlog at the West Coast and the possibility of a flood," a CWB statement said.
Three times the average amount of snow fell in the Red River basin in the United States and twice the average amount fell on the Canadian side of the basin this winter.
Manitoba Natural Resources forecast a 10 percent chance this would be the worst Red River flood of the century.

The CWB allocated enough railcars last spring to move 100,000 tonnes of grain out of the Red River Valley but a weather and equipment induced backlog of ships since January on Canada's Pacific coast may mean some grain is at risk.
"Due to extremely poor grain movement over the past three months, it is unlikely that all grain will be moved out of flood prone areas," the CWB warned.
